name: GDFWR - Frame Window Recorder
description: Records a run, proves it by replay, and measures the frame window of every click.

auto-save.name: Auto-save recordings
auto-save.description: Write a finished or partial recording to the gdfwr folder automatically.

show-hud.name: Show recording HUD
show-hud.description: Small text in the top-left corner while recording (REC, number of actions).

click-between-steps.name: Clicks are exact to 1 tick
click-between-steps.description: Turn this on when you play with click-between-frames/steps. Otherwise the mod assumes a click is only exact to 240 / FPS ticks and marks the file COARSE_INPUT.

max-checkpoints.name: Max saved states (at once)
max-checkpoints.description: How many saved game states are kept at the same time while the clicks are measured (they use memory; lower this on a phone). A macro with more click edges than this is NOT refused: it is measured in parts, and the level is replayed once per part. Never lower than 8 in practice.

auto-repair.name: Fit the clicks to the game when the macro does not pass
auto-repair.description: A recording made at a low frame rate is only exact to one frame, so a click can be a few ticks off. When the player dies during the check, the click that was active is moved by the smallest amount that gets the run past that point (+1, -1, +2, -2 ... ticks) until the run reaches the end of the level. Every moved click is listed in the result (recorded -> now) and Edit clicks > Restore all brings the recorded ticks back. Off = the check just reports the failure.

repair-max-shift.name: Fit: largest shift (ticks)
repair-max-shift.description: How far a click is moved in each direction before giving up. It is never smaller than one frame of the recording (240 / FPS ticks) plus 2, so a recording made at 14 FPS is searched 19 ticks each way whatever this says.

search-reach.name: Search beyond 12 ticks (up to)
search-reach.description: Every window is tested tick by tick up to 12 ticks on each side. A side that passes all of those is searched on up to this many ticks (steps of 4, then bisected), so wide windows get an exact value instead of 12+. 12 = off (fastest). Higher values save a second state per click edge, so very long macros reach the \"Max saved states\" limit sooner.

whole-click-window.name: Press window moves the release too (old rule)
whole-click-window.description: Default off: the press window moves only the press and the release window only the release, each action on its own. On = the v0.1 rule: the press window moves press and release together (the hold stays the same).

count-untrusted-recording.name: Count clicks of a recording with a flagged tick counter
count-untrusted-recording.description: On (default): the windows are measured by replaying the level, so a flagged tick counter or input of the RECORDING (UNRELIABLE_TICK, UNRELIABLE_INPUT) does not stop a click from being counted; the check and the fit have already proved that the macro, as it is now, passes. Off = the old rule: every click near such a flag is marked UNRELIABLE and not counted.

fast-converge.name: Stop a run that is back on the verified run
fast-converge.description: On (default): when a moved click leads to exactly the same game state as the verified run for 4 ticks in a row, the rest of the run is the verified run, so it is not simulated any further. Much faster; the windows are the same. Off = every run is simulated up to the next click.

full-scan-top.name: Tick-by-tick scan of the tightest clicks
full-scan-top.description: After the measurement, this many of the tightest clicks are scanned again tick by tick on both sides (pass map, holes and traps). 0 (default) = off: the window counts do not need it, and it about doubles the time.

precision-readout.name: Show precision readout
precision-readout.description: Raw Precision (24h) in sigma/s at the bottom left of the replay. PROVISIONAL: the model is not confirmed yet.

ring-hold.name: Ring: seconds fully visible
ring-hold.description: A ring appears at once (no animation) and stays at full strength for this long. A ring that stays in the level scrolls off the screen in about a second at normal speed, so the two times matter mostly in slow parts, or when the setting "Ring stays in the level" is off.

ring-fade.name: Ring: seconds of fading
ring-fade.description: After the time above the ring fades out slowly over this many seconds.

ring-follow-level.name: Ring stays in the level
ring-follow-level.description: On (default): a ring is fixed in the level at the place of the click or release and scrolls away with the level. Off: it stays where it appeared on the screen until it has faded. (The grey "any" ring, a release that never mattered, is not shown at all.)

ring-sound.name: Play a sound when a ring appears
ring-sound.description: Plays classic.wav for every ring with a measured window; the grey ? ring is silent. Every label has its own pitch: set it with the blue Ring pitch button in the GDFWR panel, or with the small blue ring above the counters during a replay.
